value.name: Miles claims the items are gifts
value.description: Miles insists that the expensive items he received from clients are merely gifts.
evidence: Stuff you get from grateful clients.

value.name: Marilyn labels the gifts unreported income
value.description: Marilyn rejects Miles's explanation and frames the items as taxable, undeclared income.

value.name: Marilyn checks the time on Bellagio Road
value.description: Marilyn glances at her watch and asks what time it is on Bellagio Road, implying concern about another location or schedule.
evidence: (Glancing at his watch) By the way, what time IS it on Bellagio Road?

value.name: Miles denies wrongdoing
value.description: Miles responds defensively that Marilyn cannot prove any illegal conduct.

value.name: Marilyn invokes IRS enforcement
value.description: Marilyn says she does not need proof herself because IRS agents handle such cases aggressively.
evidence: MARYLIN I don't have to. That's what the IRS guys do. And they do it with great zeal.

value.name: Marilyn explains IRS resentment
value.description: Marilyn describes IRS workers as bitter and vengeful toward wealthy lawyers who treat their work as a source of luxury perks.
evidence: See, they work at these tortuous civil service jobs, and when five hundred dollar an hour boys like you take their trade out in luxury goodies, these saps feel.. well, they feel like saps. And they feel bitter and they feel vengeful and they feel WRATH.

value.name: Marilyn smokes Miles's cigar
value.description: Marilyn puffs on Miles's cigar while mocking it as a Romeo y Julieta.
evidence: (Puffing on the cigar) What is this? A Romeo and Julieta?
